# 2026 Spanish Grand Prix Madrid Schedule & Timetable
The 2026 Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid is the 16th round of the Formula 1 championship and will be held on the Friday 11th to Sunday 13th September at the new Madring circuit in Madrid.

## 2026 Spanish GP dates
The Spanish Grand Prix has a new home from 2026 onwards. It’s no longer held at the [Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya,](https://oversteer48.com/barcelona-catalunya-grand-prix-schedule/) instead it moves to the new Madring street circuit in Madrid.

...

## Madring Grand Prix race weekend format
The 2026 Spanish GP will have the usual format of three practice sessions, qualifying session and then the full grand prix. There is no sprint race.
Below is the format and duration of the different F1 sessions during the race weekend:
**Friday 11th September:**
* Practice 1 (60 mins)
* Practice 2 (60 mins)
**Saturday 12th September:**
* Practice 3 (60 mins)
* Qualifying – Q1 / Q2 / Q3 (60 mins)
**Sunday 13th September:**
* Grand Prix (120 mins / 66 laps)

## Edd Straw
But the introduction of the 2026 engines might change that, albeit only temporarily, with Mercedes trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin suggesting there will be “more jeopardy” thanks to the risk of reliability troubles throughout the field next year.
The last two F1 seasons have been the most reliable in grand prix history. The retirement rate across both 2024 and 2025 was just 10.5%, when measured by proportion of starters to be classified finishers - and in both cases the majority of those were down to driver errors rather than an engine blowing up or something breaking.
While the days when half the field or more might fail to finish won’t return - the last of those was in 1994 when the retirement rate was 51.8% - there should at least be a little more unpredictability on this side of things early in the year.

Even in the 21st century, rule changes have tended to lead to an increase in retirements. When the 1.6-litre V6 turbo hybrid engines were adopted in 2014, the retirement rate was 20.8%. That in itself seemed impossibly low during the first pre-season test at Jerez that year, when running was so limited.
In 2022, when the ground-effect cars that have just been retired made their debut, the retirement rate was 16.9%, which was a step back from the 12.6% managed the year before. When the wider, high-downforce cars were brought in for 2017, the retirement rate jumped from 17.3% to 23%.

Antonelli now leads Russell by 66 points in the drivers' championship, nearly three grands prix worth.

The driver, who spun before hitting the barriers at Turn 19, emerged uninjured from the accident and managed to climb out of his cockpit on his own, even though the rear of his car was already on fire.
The session was halted for around half an hour to allow time to clean the track and repair the safety barrier that had absorbed the impact.
It follows last month's testing by F3 drivers which saw 19 red flags across two days, albeit not all of them were for crashes, and concerns from Formula One drivers ahead of Sunday's race.
"When I heard about the 20 red flags in Formula 3, I was a bit surprised," said Mercedes's George Russell on Thursday.
"But when I then drove the circuit in the simulator, I was actually more surprised that there were only 20 red flags. It's a mad circuit.
"I'd even go so far as to say it's the riskiest track on the entire calendar."
Madring has 22 corners and features blind turns and an impressive banked corner of up to 24 degrees called 'La Monumental'.
"I'll put my money on a red flag," said Alpine's Pierre Gasly.
The semi-permanent circuit winds around Ifema, Madrid's exhibition centre, and is located to the north of the city, near Real Madrid's training complex and Barajas Airport.
F1 drivers will get a first taste of the circuit during the opening free practice session later Friday.
